Sara — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few sizing clarifications so we can give a firm dedicated capacity recommendation.

Recap: Acme AI will evaluate Redwood Dedicated for the SummarizePro feature (multi-doc RAG + LLM). You indicated the priority is predictable latency at peak + cost visibility. You prefer private H100 fleet if feasible but are open to A100 tradeoffs.

Open items I need to size this:
- Target sustained RPS and peak burst RPS (please include 1m and 5m peaks).
- Concurrency: typical concurrent requests during peak.
- Token mix: avg prompt tokens vs avg completion tokens, and 90th pct sequence length.
- Desired p95 latency SLO (ms).
- Model we should size for (e.g., Llama-70B, MPT-30B).

Action: if you can reply with the numbers below, I’ll run two sizing options (H100 and A100) and send an estimate + recommended autoscale policy and cost delta. I’ve attached a quick capacity estimate template for your convenience.

Thanks —

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Answers below (numbers are approximate, happy to refine):

- Sustained RPS: 25 req/s average (we measure at 1m granularity).
- Peak burst: 80 req/s (5m sustained), with brief spikes to ~120 req/s for <1m.
- Typical concurrency at peak: ~60 concurrent in-flight requests (this accounts for longer tail completions).
- Token mix: avg prompt 400 tokens, avg completion 150 tokens (so ~550 tokens total). 90th percentile sequence length ~1,200 tokens.
- Model: planning to test with a 70B-class open model (Llama-70B or equivalent).
- Desired p95 latency: <= 600 ms.

We have some prefix caching opportunity — about 20% of requests hit a cached retrieval prefix (shorter prompt paths).

Timeline: pilot in ~6 weeks, production in 10–12 weeks if sizing and pricing align.

Let us know what you recommend for GPU count and whether H100 is required for the SLO.

—Sara

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & sizing questions — Dedicated capacity

Sara — thanks for the details, very helpful. Initial sizing notes below (high-level estimates; Rafael and I will validate with a micro-benchmark during the deep-dive):

Sizing assumptions:
- Model: Llama-70B (dense); sequence length baseline 1,024, 90th pct 1,200.
- Token mix: avg 550 tokens/request (400 prompt + 150 completion).
- Target p95: 600 ms.
- Workload: average 25 RPS, 5m sustained peak 80 RPS, burst to 120 RPS.
- KV cache & caching: 20% hit rate reduces avg tokens for those requests by ~40%.

Option A — H100 (recommended for smaller GPU count & headroom):
- Estimated baseline throughput per H100 (70B, seq ~1k, p95 ~600ms): ~12–15 RPS sustained (depends on batching behavior).
- To cover 80 RPS sustained + headroom for spikes and autoscale buffer: 6 H100 GPUs (3 pods x 2 GPUs) with autoscale to 8 for peak bursts.
- Expected p95 with autoscaling and prefix caching: ~450–600 ms.

Option B — A100 80GB (cost-optimized if you can accept more machines):
- Estimated throughput per A100: ~7–9 RPS (for same model/seq).
- GPUs needed: ~10–12 A100s to meet sustained 80 RPS, autoscale to ~14 for bursts.
- p95 will be similar at scale but operational footprint larger.

Operational recommendations:
- Start pilot on 6 H100s with autoscale policy (scale up at 70 RPS sustained for 2m, immediate autoscale for >100 RPS spikes).
- Enable prefix/KV caching and short-circuit cached responses — we estimate ~20% cost reduction for hit rate you mentioned.
- Use per-route batching config to limit request latency while benefiting from continuous batching (max batch latency 40 ms).
- Plan a technical deep-dive next week for micro-benchmarks: Rafael will run an internal benchmark against the target model and token mix.

I’ve attached a quick cost/throughput workbook and a Redwood Dedicated pricing summary. If you confirm model (Llama-70B) and the token numbers above, I’ll finalize a formal quote and dedicated capacity proposal.

Next steps:
1) Confirm model + token mix (reply).
2) Schedule 60m technical deep-dive (Rafael + infra).
3) We’ll deliver a micro-benchmark and a firm GPU count + pricing.

Thanks —
Marissa
